BUG. In shadow_report.py `_join`, `turn_would_reject` starts as `not isinstance(shadow, dict) or shadow.get('outcome') != 'ok'`. For an observation turn with ZERO relations the shadow outcome is 'no_relations' (or the shadow record may be missing), so the turn is counted as one enforcement would reject, which inflates the original gate clause 2 (good-turn strict reject rate) and the mixed-turn counts. A turn with zero relations is never rejected by enforcement (nothing is asked). Fix: `turn_would_reject` can be True only when the turn has at least one relation (a relation verdict that is not 'accept', or a shadow outcome other than 'ok', or a missing shadow record, all evaluated only when relations is non-empty). Zero-relation turns still count in `good_turns` (all labels true vacuously) but never as rejected; keep the 2b logic as is. Also make sure `turns_without_shadow` still reports them. 

TESTS FIRST in tests/test_shadow_report.py: a synthetic set containing zero-relation turns with outcome 'no_relations' and with a missing shadow record -> clause 2 good-turn reject count excludes them (compute the exact expected counts), and the printed good-turn rejection rate matches; a turn with relations and outcome 'unavailable' is still a rejection. Keep all existing tests green. FINISH: ruff check and format; report counts.
